title: Social Life
description: Travel, sport and the people you meet: name the kinds of journey (a trip, a flight, an excursion, a voyage) and read the documents that sell them (a brochure, a leaflet, galleries, jewellery, to broaden, to amaze); say what is possible and give advice with can, could, may, might, you should, why not and how about; add a second negative fact with either at the end of the sentence, against too in an affirmative one and against the short replies so do I and neither do I; ask about and express satisfaction or dissatisfaction with an interviewer's questions (How do you feel about…? Are you satisfied with…?) and the words of the game (a league, teammates, a coach, a career, to cheer, to miss, to look forward to, grateful, eager); build the present perfect progressive with have or has been + verb-ing to insist on an activity that has lasted and is still going on, with since for the starting point, for for the length and How long have you been…? for the question, against the present perfect simple that counts finished results; and hear which syllable of a word carries the strong beat — plus the three cross-cutting reflexes of Progress Check 1: word formation, punctuation and capitals, and linkers
